items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: the owner of the club was a nice guy to work for, Billy Berg

ctx.x: And you played in the Swing Club in Hollywood. Any impressions of the music scene in the West Coast at that time?

No, it was during the war, you know, and the only thing I do remember, I had Buddy Rich on drums for a couple of weeks while he was awaiting his greetings. [laughter] But beyond that, no, I don’t remember anything. You know, naturally there were sailors and soldiers from time to time, but other than that the clientele was quite ordinary, the usual jazz lover or music lover. It was a nice room to work in, and the owner of the club was a nice guy to work for, Billy Berg [phonetic].

You mentioned it was during the war, and at this time you began to do a lot of work entertaining troops, making armed forces broadcasts. Did people approach you to do that or did you volunteer it or was it . . .

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: Actually, while I was working on the film, we were playing at the Billy Berg Swing Billie Burke Street Club. For Billy Berg.

ctx.x: And that was on Las Palmas Avenue at Hollywood Boulevard. Actually, a little bit north of Hollywood Boulevard. Run by a man named Billy Berg. My manager at that time was Carlos Castell, who was also the manager of Stan Kenton, and I believe, Sonny Dunham's orchestra --and we went in to this club -- I think we were booked in for 2 weeks, and it seems to me we stayed 8; did tremendous business there, and during the time I was there, they were making a film at 20th Century Fox called "Stormy Weather."
